start: ^Rain had washed the street black by the time I reached the short-let apartment. The patrol car outside kept its lights off. That told me the body was fresh, the neighbors were awake, and somebody in uniform still hoped the night could be kept quiet.
^My name was Antonio Luna. I worked homicide, which meant I had learned to distrust rooms that looked almost clean.

^Officer Ben Pike met me at the door. Dr. Maeve Ibarra was already in the bathroom with the dead man. In the living room, a young woman sat under a weak lamp and held a tissue that had never touched her eyes.
^Her name was Clara Voss. She said she had loved Javier Morrow. She said a lot of things.
apartment_nav: ^The apartment waited around me: living room and kitchenette, bedroom, bathroom. Three rooms, one corpse, and one woman who kept her grief too carefully folded.
notebook: ^I opened my notebook and took stock.

b: ^Clara had been placed in the bathroom by the earring evidence.
^I still needed to place Clara inside the bathroom.
^The scarf and the ligature mark gave me the method.
^I still needed to prove how Javier had died.
^The blackmail papers gave me Clara's motive.
^I still needed a motive strong enough for murder.

notebook: ^The trick in murder was not finding facts. It was making the facts stand close enough together that the lie had nowhere left to breathe.
accuse_clara: ^I stood over Clara. She looked up slowly, as if my shadow had taken too much of the room.

b: ^"You were in the bathroom," I said. "Your earring back was in the basin trap, and you were missing the pearl that matched it."
^"You strangled Javier with your scarf. Dr. Ibarra found the ligature mark, and the scarf was in the kitchenette trash because you needed it out of sight."
^"And he was blackmailing you. Lisbon gallery money, a bank transfer, a deadline. He brought the proof. You brought the scarf."
^For a moment the rain did all the talking.
^"He said he would ruin me," Clara said at last. Her voice had lost the polish. "He laughed when I begged. I only meant to stop him talking."
^"People always say that after they stop someone breathing."
^Pike moved in, cuffs ready. Clara did not fight. The room seemed smaller after the confession, as if the apartment had only been rented for that one lie and now the lease had expired.
^I had not yet proved she entered the bathroom.
^I had not yet tied the death to a weapon.
^I had not yet found the motive.
^"Detective," she said, "I know you need someone to blame. But I sat right here. Javier went in alone."
^It was a good lie because it was small. I went back to the rooms and looked for the parts that did not fit.

^The living room had been arranged by someone who thought temporary meant innocent. A gray sofa faced a television no one had turned on. The kitchenette ran along one wall: two stools, a short counter, a sink bright with recent wiping.

^Clara Voss sat under the lamp with one knee crossed over the other. One pearl earring shone at her left ear. The right ear showed only a small red mark where its twin should have been.
^The living room still smelled of rainwater, gin, and the lemon cleaner somebody had used too late.

living_room: ^Return to the center of the apartment.

c-0: ^Her hair was pinned back on one side. The missing right earring was not a fashion choice; the skin there was freshly rubbed, as if the clasp had been torn away.

b: ^The little pearl back from the bathroom had just found its owner.

c-1: ^Beneath coffee pods and a paper sleeve from a bottle of tonic, I found a blue silk scarf twisted into a tight rope. One end was damp. The other carried a faint brown smear that was not makeup.

b: ^I did not need poetry to see the shape of it. I needed Maeve to make it speak in court.

c-2:
^There were two glasses on the counter. Javier's held a thumbprint in condensation. Clara's was dry, lipstick bright on the rim, placed where she could reach it from the sofa.

^The arrangement said she had staged stillness after movement. It did not say enough by itself.

b: ^The bedroom was narrow, white, and impersonal. Javier's overnight bag sat open on the bed. A shirt hung from one drawer like a man trying to climb out.
^The bedroom had not changed. Cheap rooms rarely did; they only became less convincing.

bedroom: ^Inspect the room for signs of struggle.
^Return to the center of the apartment.

c-0: ^In the inside pocket I found a brown envelope marked with Clara's name. It held photocopies from a Lisbon gallery account: transfers, missing donations, a signature that looked too much like hers.

b: ^The papers and the transfer gave the motive a spine.

c-1: ^Javier's phone was unlocked by whatever arrogance had killed him. The last message was ready but unsent: "Tonight. Ten thousand more, or I take the gallery file to police."

b: ^Blackmail had stepped out of suggestion and into evidence.

c-2: ^The bedspread was smooth. The lamp was upright. If Javier had fought, he had done it elsewhere, close enough to water and tile for someone to sell the wrong story.

b: ^The bathroom was all white tile and bad light. Javier Morrow lay half turned beside the tub, one hand open against the floor. Dr. Maeve Ibarra crouched beside him with her gloves already dark at the fingertips.
^The bathroom gave back the same cold light. Javier waited in it with the patience of the dead.

bathroom: ^Return to the center of the apartment.

c-0: ^Maeve angled the lamp. Under the jaw, almost hidden by shaving shadow, ran a narrow bruised line.
^"Not a fall," she said. "Pressure. Soft material, pulled hard."
c-1: ^A pearl earring back glittered in the bend of the basin trap. I lifted it with tweezers and let it rest in an evidence sleeve, tiny as a period at the end of a sentence.

b: ^The missing earring in the living room had just placed Clara where she swore she had never been.

c-2: ^The towel on the rail was dry. The bath mat was wet only near Javier's shoulder. Someone had added disorder after the body stopped being able to object.

clara_dialogue: ^Clara looked smaller when I stood near her, but not weaker. There was a difference. Weak people trembled by accident. Clara chose when to tremble.

c-0: ^"Javier was drunk," she said. "He went to the bathroom to wash his face. I stayed here. I heard a noise, then I screamed for help."
^"Not until the officer came. I could not bear to look."
c-1: ^I showed her the evidence sleeve. "This came from the bathroom sink. You're missing its twin."
^Clara touched her bare ear too late.
^"Javier took it," she said. "He was playing with it while we drank. He must have carried it in there."
^It was a lie with fresh paint. I wrote it down anyway.
c-2: ^Clara looked toward the kitchenette and found the distance longer than she expected.
^"Javier spilled gin on it," she said. "I threw it away. It was ruined."

b:
^"Dr. Ibarra says soft material crushed his throat."

^"Then someone else used it." She gave me the answer too fast. "Someone came in while I was crying."
^I let the lie sit. Without the medical connection, it was only ugly cloth in a bin.

c-3: ^"He had gallery files with your name on them," I said. "And a message demanding ten thousand more."
^For the first time, Clara forgot to look sad.
^"He was helping me," she said. "I made mistakes. He said he knew a lawyer."
^She folded the tissue until it became a hard white square.
c-4: ^Silence bothered her more than accusation. She filled it with a small breath, a glance at the bathroom door, a hand drifting to the bare ear and stopping halfway.

maeve_dialogue: ^Dr. Maeve Ibarra did not look up until she had finished bagging a trace sample. Maeve believed the dead deserved complete sentences.
^Show her the scarf from the trash.
^Ask what kind of weapon to look for.
^Ask whether the scene fits an accident.

c-0: ^"He was not killed by the fall," she said. "There is a ligature mark under the jaw. Soft material. Narrow pull. Strong pressure."
^"Not from that angle, and not with those bruises."
c-1: ^Maeve took the scarf without drama. She matched its width with the mark on Javier's throat and gave me the look she used when uncertainty had run out of room.
^"This could have done it," she said. "If the lab gives me skin cells or fibers, I will say it louder."
^The method was no longer a shadow.
c-2:
^"Soft," Maeve said. "A towel, scarf, belt, maybe a cord wrapped in fabric. Something that could vanish into domestic clutter."

^In a rented apartment, domestic clutter came prearranged.
c-3: ^"No," Maeve said. "The body was moved. The wet marks are too selective, and the towel is dry where it should not be. Someone wanted a fall. They did not earn one."

pike_dialogue: ^Officer Pike stood near the door with his notebook open and his face set in the brave expression of a man hoping procedure could hold the world together.

c-0: ^"Neighbor downstairs heard a thump at 12:18," Pike said. "Call came in at 12:21. I arrived at 12:28. The chain was not on, no sign of forced entry."
^"No one I saw. Hall camera is dead, because of course it is."
c-1:
^"She said she sat on the sofa the whole time," Pike said. "Said he went to the bathroom alone. She was very clear about not touching anything."

^People who were very clear before they had been accused always interested me.
c-2:
^Pike shook his head. "No forced entry, no open window, no extra glass, no neighbor saw another visitor. If someone else did it, they came through a wall."

^I had yet to arrest a wall.
